title: refactor(lodash): remove find usage
body:
This removes all `lodash/find` usages. We need to be careful with `undefined` collections being loop over since Lodash used to deal with that for us.

Note that we already use `Array.prototype.find` in the codebase and that we document [using a polyfill to support browsers](https://www.algolia.com/doc/guides/building-search-ui/installation/js/#browser-support).

@samouss Do you mean that it would be safer to create our own util?

Yes, I'd go for polyfill here too for the reasons discussed by @samouss. This is likely going to break implementations since we didn't use it visibly before. Especially since it's easy to use indexOf instead of find

That would make sense to me.

When you say "polyfill", you mean an actual polyfill or a wrapper function?

We shouldn't polyfill, but instead use our own util function which uses indexOf. The real polyfill on MDN seems more advanced, but not things we really need: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/find#Polyfill (it also has a note about not polyfilling)

I created a `find` util function that uses the native `find` method if available, otherwise an implementation with `filter`.

I chose to keep the native one when available because it's optimized to return once the item is found (it doesn't go through all items).

If you're concerned about the `reduce` implementation which goes through all the items, we can refactor it with a basic loop.

Once this is merged, we can remove the `find` mention in the Browser support section of the documentation.
